newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-PacifiCorp agrees bid for Energy Group.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-PacifiCorp agrees bid for Energy Group.

text.p: U.S. group PacifiCorp on Friday made a recommended 3.7 billion pound ($6 billion) bid for Britain's biggest electricity distributor The Energy Group which, if successful, would create one of the world's most powerful energy companies.

The combined company will have a total 17,000 megaWatts of generation capacity and more than 10 billion tons of coal reserves with five million electric and gas customers world wide if the deal goes through.

"This powerful combination positions the combined group as a premier global energy company with significant presence on three continents," PacifiCorp president and chief executive Fred Buckman said in a statement.
But regulatory concerns kept Energy Group's shares at a discount to the offer price of 6.955 pence, analysts said.
A 30 percent increase in Energy Group's first half to March 31 underlying operational profit to 317 million pounds was overshadowed by the bid confirmation.
On Friday, Energy Group shares were up three pence to 650 pence, around seven percent below the offer price compared with usual discounts of five percent.
"There's much more uncertainty over this deal, with a new and untried Labour government and the possibility of a windfall tax," said one analyst who asked not to be identified.

Energy Group, which includes Britain's biggest electricity supplier Eastern Electricity and U.S.-Australian coal producer Peabody, has been tipped as a takeover target since it was spun off from once-mighty industrial conglomerate Hanson Plc in February.
The company was forced to announce that it was in talks over a possible agreed offer on Tuesday after its share price rose strongly on the stock exchange.

PacifiCorp said it would sell its Pacific Telecom unit for $1.5 billion to Century Telephone Enterprises Inc as part of the move and would assume Energy Group's $3.8 billion of debt, valuing the deal at $9.6 billion in debt and equity.

PacifiCorp, a diversified energy company in the U.S. and Australia, is making the offer for the Energy Group, which has interests in Britain, the U.S. and Australia, through its unit PacifiCorp Holdings Inc.
Analysts had said earlier in the week that a bid around seven pounds per share would look reasonable but had cautioned that regulatory uncertainty could trim price levels.

The new Labour government, which swept to power in a landslide victory on May 1, was fiercely critical of the previous government's takeover policy which saw all but one of the original 12 regional electricity companies (Recs) swallowed up by buyers.
Privatised utilities also face a one-off tax on excess profits which the government has vowed to include in its first budget on July 2.
Uncertainty over which companies would be hit by the tax and by how much has kept utility sector shares under pressure in recent months, with many trading at discounts to the market.
But analysts said there was scant reason on competition or regulatory grounds for the new Labour government to block a takeover.
"I can't see any obvious problems for the government. The Rec has already been taken over so largely it's just a change of ownership rather than structure," the analyst said.
Some analysts believed the new government might call for customer compensation in the form of price cuts in order to approve the bid.
Recs have proved very attractive to U.S. buyers who are keen to gain experience of operating in a liberalised and regulated market, as Britain plans to open up to domestic competition in 1998.

"The Energy Group's large, diverse customer base, expertise in energy trading and risk management and industry-leading position in coal strategically complement PacifiCorp's competitive strengths in fuel management, low-cost power generation and bulk power marketing," PacifiCorp president and chief executive Fred Buckman said in a statement.
The merger is expected to enhance earnings for PacifiCorp from the first year following completion, the company said.
Energy Group chairman Derek Bonham and chief executive John Devaney are expected to join PacifiCorp's board of directors. ($ = 0.613 British Pounds)
